title: Sourdough Starter
body: A sourdough starter is a mixture of flour and water in which wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria grow. The baker feeds the starter with fresh flour and water once or twice a day to keep the culture active.

title: Levain
body: A levain is a portion of sourdough starter that the baker feeds, leaves to ripen for several hours and then mixes into the final dough to make it rise.

title: Autolyse
body: Autolyse is a rest of 20 to 60 minutes after flour and water are first mixed and before salt and levain are added. During the rest the flour absorbs the water and gluten begins to form.

title: Bulk Fermentation
body: Bulk fermentation is the first rise of the whole dough after mixing. The yeast produces carbon dioxide, the bacteria produce acids, and the baker folds the dough at intervals to build its strength.

title: Dough Hydration
body: The hydration of a dough is the weight of its water divided by the weight of its flour, given as a percentage. A dough of 1000 grams of flour and 750 grams of water has a hydration of 75 percent.

title: Oven Spring
body: Oven spring is the fast rise of a sourdough loaf in the first minutes of baking, when the heat expands the gas in the dough before the crust sets.

title: Banneton
body: A banneton is a basket that holds shaped sourdough during its final proof and gives the loaf its form.

title: Tidal Force
body: A tidal force is the difference between the gravitational pull of the Moon or the Sun on the side of the Earth facing it and on the far side. The difference stretches the oceans into two bulges.

title: Spring Tide
body: A spring tide occurs near new moon and full moon, when the Sun, the Moon and the Earth are in line and their tidal forces add, so the tidal range is at its largest.

title: Neap Tide
body: A neap tide occurs near the first and the last quarter moon, when the Sun and the Moon pull at right angles to each other, so the tidal range is at its smallest.

title: Tidal Range
body: The tidal range is the vertical difference between the sea level at high tide and the sea level at the following low tide.

title: Semidiurnal Tide
body: A semidiurnal tide has two high waters and two low waters in each lunar day, which lasts about 24 hours and 50 minutes.

title: Tide Gauge
body: A tide gauge is an instrument fixed at the coast that records the sea level over time.

title: Amphidromic Point
body: An amphidromic point is a place in the ocean where the tidal range is close to zero and around which the tide rotates.
